lines.text: Many learners say: I asked a pizza at the cafe.
Better: I ordered a pizza at the cafe.
In a cafe, you order food.
Ordered! I ordered a pizza at the cafe.

data.wrong: I asked a pizza at the cafe.
data.right: I ordered a pizza at the cafe.
data.why: In a cafe, you order food.

quiz.stem: I ___ a pizza at the cafe.

native.tip: En español “pedir” sirve para todo, pero en inglés la comida se pide con “order”.
native.caption: 🙈 Error común: “I asked a pizza at the cafe.” “Pedir” comida se dice “order”, no “ask”: “I ordered a pizza at the cafe.” ¡Escucha a Ama y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “ordered”. “Ask” es para preguntas; para pedir comida o bebida se usa “order”. Escribe una frase tuya con “ordered” o dila en voz alta: {link}

en.tip: Learners use “pedir” for everything, but English orders food with “order.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “I asked a pizza at the cafe.” “Pedir” food is “order”, not “ask”: “I ordered a pizza at the cafe.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
